chains.title: GATA3 binds the T risk allele more strongly at the same TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: GATA3 is predicted to bind the alt T allele more strongly than the ref C allele. GATA3 has its own QBiC-SELEX model at this base with a positive alt-allele effect (effect 0.783, z 10.91), and GATA3 has ENCODE ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant in MCF7 and is very highly expressed there. The QBiC-SELEX effect is in vitro and the ChIP evidence is peak-level, not allele-specific at this base.

The variant lies in EH38E3180851, a distal enhancer-like cCRE with active chromatin and cofactor occupancy, consistent with a GATA3-occupied regulatory element. The E03 chromatin z-scores are maxima across ENCODE biosamples, not MCF7-specific.

TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene at 17.5 kb and the best L2G gene in breast cancer credible sets. No significant GTEx v8 eQTL is reported for this SNP, so the enhancer-to-TOX3 assignment is indirect.
GATA3 is very highly expressed in MCF7 and has MCF7 ChIP-seq peaks containing this variant, matching the breast luminal cell context.

The alt T allele is the risk allele in strong breast cancer GWAS and in a meta-analysis, giving a disease direction in which T increases risk. One E15 maternal breast-cancer entry uses effect allele C and would need harmonization.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP or footprinting at this base in MCF7 or another C/T heterozygous breast cancer line should show stronger GATA3 occupancy on T than C.
In an enhancer reporter in MCF7, the T-vs-C activity difference should be sensitive to mutation of the GATA3 motif if GATA3 mediates the effect; activity direction could be activation or repression.
If GATA3 acts through this element, CRISPR allele swap from C to T should change TOX3 expression or enhancer activity in a GATA3-dependent way.
falsified_if: GATA3 ChIP or footprinting is not allele-specific at this base in breast cancer cells.
The T-vs-C enhancer activity difference remains after GATA3 motif mutation or GATA3 depletion.
The GATA3 ChIP peak over the variant is not resolved to the variant base or is not seen in breast contexts.

chains.title: FOXA1 binds the T risk allele more strongly at a TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: FOXA1 is predicted to bind the alt T allele more strongly than the ref C allele. FOXA1 has its own QBiC-SELEX model at this base with a positive alt-allele effect (effect 0.314, z 9.34), and FOXA1 has ENCODE ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant in MCF7 and is highly expressed there. This is still a motif-plus-occupancy prediction, not allele-specific occupancy measured at this base.

The variant lies in EH38E3180851, a distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase, H3K27ac and active-element cofactor ChIP signal, so it is a plausible regulatory element rather than a coding change. The E03 chromatin z-scores are maxima across ENCODE biosamples, not MCF7-specific.

TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene at 17.5 kb and is the best L2G gene in breast cancer credible sets. There is no significant GTEx v8 eQTL for this SNP, so the enhancer-to-TOX3 link rests on proximity, L2G and literature, not a direct expression QTL.
MCF7 is a relevant breast cancer context: FOXA1 is highly expressed in DepMap MCF7 and FOXA1 ChIP-seq peaks in MCF7 contain this variant.

The alt T allele is the risk allele in the strongest breast cancer GWAS associations and in a meta-analysis, giving a disease direction in which T increases risk. One E15 maternal breast-cancer entry uses effect allele C and would need harmonization.

predictions: Allele-specific FOXA1 ChIP or footprinting at this base in MCF7 or another C/T heterozygous breast cancer line should show stronger FOXA1 occupancy on T than C.
In an enhancer reporter in MCF7, the T-vs-C activity difference should be sensitive to mutation of the FOXA1 motif if FOXA1 mediates the effect; activity direction could be activation or repression.
If FOXA1 acts through this element, CRISPR allele swap from C to T should change TOX3 expression or enhancer activity in a FOXA1-dependent way.
falsified_if: FOXA1 ChIP or footprinting is not allele-specific at this base in breast cancer cells.
The T-vs-C enhancer activity difference remains after FOXA1 motif mutation or FOXA1 depletion.
Allele-specific FOXA1 binding is seen only outside breast contexts and not in MCF7 or breast tumors.

chains.title: No TF-mediated allelic effect at this base
predictions: There is no allele-specific occupancy or activity at this exact base for FOXA1, GATA3 or other candidate TFs.
The breast cancer association is explained by a linked causal variant in the same credible set or by haplotype effects rather than by rs4784227 itself.
CRISPR allele swap at rs4784227 alone should not change TOX3 expression or enhancer activity in MCF7.
falsified_if: Allele-specific TF binding and enhancer activity are demonstrated at this base in breast cells.
CRISPR editing of rs4784227 alone changes TOX3 expression or a breast cancer-relevant phenotype.
The variant is shown to be the causal base within the credible set rather than a passenger or linked marker.

grades_v0.reason: E05/E04 show FOXA1 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant in MCF-7, so occupancy evidence exists. However, the QBiC-SELEX alt-binding effect in E21 is from a CIS-BP-mapped FOXA2 model, not FOXA1's own model, and there is no allele-specific ChIP, footprinting, MPRA, or CRISPR assay at this base. Occupancy plus a paralog motif prediction does not directly show FOXA1 binds T more than C.

E01/E03 place the variant in EH38E3180851, a dELS distal enhancer-like cCRE, and E04 reports active-element cofactor ChIP peaks containing the variant. Caveat: E03 z-scores are maxima across ENCODE biosamples, not MCF-7-specific.

E02 places TOX3 17.5 kb away and E16 gives strong breast-cancer L2G to TOX3 (0.92-0.96), but E17 reports no GTEx v8 eQTL and no enhancer-gene perturbation assay is cited. L2G is variant-to-gene, not enhancer-to-gene, so the TOX3 assignment is indirect.
E05 shows FOXA1 is highly expressed in DepMap MCF7 (88.38 TPM, rank 28/1626) and has MCF-7 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant; E04 also reports MCF-7 peaks at the variant.

E15 reports very strong breast-cancer associations with effect allele T, and E18b quotes a meta-analysis with OR > 1 for T versus C. Direction is T = risk and T = more binding, consistent. One E15 maternal breast-cancer entry uses effect allele C and would need harmonization.

E06/E04 show GATA3 ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant in MCF-7, but E20's QBiC-SELEX alt-binding effect uses a CIS-BP-mapped GATA2 model, not GATA3's own model, and no allele-specific occupancy or reporter assay is cited. The direction is consistent but the binding-change evidence for GATA3 itself is indirect.

E01/E03 identify the variant within the EH38E3180851 dELS enhancer, and E04 reports active cofactor occupancy containing the variant. Caveat: chromatin z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not MCF-7-specific.
TOX3 is supported as the nearest gene and by breast-cancer L2G in E02/E16, but E17 reports no GTEx v8 eQTL and no direct enhancer-gene assay is cited. The gene assignment remains proximity/L2G-based.
E06 shows GATA3 is very highly expressed in MCF7 (346.04 TPM, rank 5/1626) and has MCF-7 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant.
E15 and E18b support T as the breast-cancer risk allele with increased risk. Direction is consistent with the claimed T-allele gain of binding. The same E15 effect-allele caveat applies.

E07/E04 show SPDEF ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant in MCF-7, but E24's QBiC-SELEX effect uses a CIS-BP-mapped ELF1 model, not SPDEF's own model. E24 also reports alt site strength lower than ref (76.3rd vs 79.2th percentile) despite a positive effect, an internal direction inconsistency. No allele-specific assay is cited.

E01/E03 place the variant in the EH38E3180851 dELS enhancer with active chromatin annotation, and E04 reports active-element cofactor occupancy. Caveat: the chromatin z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples.

E15 and E18b support T as the breast-cancer risk allele. The disease direction is supported, but it does not rescue the weak and internally inconsistent SPDEF binding evidence.

checks.why: Determines whether FOXA1 has its own QBiC-SELEX model with an alt-binding effect or whether the effect is only through the mapped FOXA2 model.
Determines whether GATA3 itself has a QBiC-SELEX alt-binding effect or whether the effect is only through the mapped GATA2 model.
Tests whether SPDEF has its own model supporting the alt-binding direction, which would help resolve the ELF1-mapped model and site-strength inconsistency.

matrix.test: Allele-specific ChIP-qPCR for FOXA1 and GATA3 at rs4784227 in a C/T heterozygous breast cancer line (or MCF7 if heterozygous), reporting T/C allelic ratios.

outcomes.outcome: FOXA1 shows a T>C allelic occupancy skew at this base; GATA3 is not required to show one.
GATA3 shows a T>C allelic occupancy skew at this base; FOXA1 is not required to show one.
Neither FOXA1 nor GATA3 shows allele-specific occupancy at this base.

matrix.test: Enhancer reporter or MPRA of the EH38E3180851 element with C vs T alleles, comparing wild-type sequence to separate FOXA1-motif and GATA3-motif mutations in MCF7.

outcomes.outcome: T-vs-C activity difference is lost or strongly reduced by FOXA1-motif mutation, but not by GATA3-motif mutation.
T-vs-C activity difference is lost or strongly reduced by GATA3-motif mutation, but not by FOXA1-motif mutation.
No reproducible T-vs-C activity difference, or any difference is not attributable to either motif.

matrix.test: CRISPR C>T allele swap at rs4784227 in MCF7 followed by TOX3 expression and enhancer-activity measurement.

outcomes.outcome: Allele swap changes TOX3 expression or enhancer activity, with FOXA1 dependence if FOXA1 is perturbed.
Allele swap changes TOX3 expression or enhancer activity, with GATA3 dependence if GATA3 is perturbed.
No change in TOX3 expression or enhancer activity after editing rs4784227 alone.

next_experiment: Allele-specific ChIP-qPCR for FOXA1 and GATA3 at rs4784227 in a C/T heterozygous breast cancer cell line, reporting T/C allelic ratios, is the cheapest single experiment that separates the top two chains.

Key examples include promoter mutations [e.g., rs2279744 (Mouse double minute 2 homolog gene; MDM2)], enhancer mutations [e.g., rs4784227 (thymocyte selection-associated high mobility group box family member 3 gene; TOX3)], and lncRNAs [e.g., HOX transcript antisense intergenic RNA (HOTAIR)] linked to progression, metastasis, and poor survival.

The pooled ORs regarding the association between the rs4784227-CASC16 polymorphism and breast cancer risk were statistically significant [T vs C: OR = 1.244, 95% CI = 1.202-1.287; TT vs CT + CC: OR = 1.407, 95% CI = 1.296-1.528; CC vs CT + TT: OR = 0.777, 95% CI = 0.745-0.811; TT vs CC: OR = 1.544, 95% CI = 1.419-1.681; CT vs CC: OR = 1.244, 95% CI = 1.189-1.301].

Our pooled analysis showed a significant association between the rs4784227- (T) allele and breast cancer susceptibility in Asian and North American populations, and intervention with this mutation might be a new therapeutic strategy for breast cancer.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr16:52565276:C>T, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000019), bound here before bound elsewhere, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 95 occupied, 5 of 75 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 45 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 411 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 22 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly.
